question: do we keep choosing the same qubits? never asked before tonight
reading: monotone decay to zero. CONFIRMS and EXTENDS F65/F66 at n=2238: the decay is SMOOTH not a cliff, and by two weeks median overlap is exactly zero. The standing rule run-live-never-cache is if anything understated.
confound_stated: different experiments need different qubit counts and connectivity, so the same-day LEVEL (0.188) mixes task variation with drift. The DECAY is the clean evidence, because task mix does not depend on the gap between flights.
artifact_caught_before_publication: a first version reported 19% of flights losing >5pp of parity fidelity, max 44pp. ARTIFACT: those cases had nq=156 (whole device — layout recovery uninformative) and dead qubits at readout ~0.50 never measured. On 94 REAL layouts: worst-qubit parity cost p50 0.24pp, p90 1.70pp, max 8.05pp, 7% losing >2pp. The picker is working well. Third instance tonight of the same set-selection error.
picker_note: scripts/quiet_qubits.py minimizes an objective-weighted SUM and reports the QUIETEST participating qubit; for a parity observable the WORST participating qubit governs. Headroom for a minimax variant is real but modest (p90 1.70pp).
